newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger on retail sales data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger on retail sales data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Thursday, rising in tandem with U.S. Treasuries, as a tame U.S. retail sales report reduced expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will soon hike rates, analysts said.

"The retail sales numbers this morning were surprising across the board on the downside," said Craig Wright, deputy chief economist with Royal Bank of Canada. "A July (Fed) move has got to be ruled out on the numbers now."
Canada's 30-year benchmark rose C$0.99 to C$115.20 to yield 6.804 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 27/32 to yield 6.77 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to three basis points from four basis points at Wednesday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened after the U.S. Commerce Department reported that retail sales fell 0.1 percent in May, compared with expectations of a 0.4 percent rise.
"The improvement in the Canadian bond market is about the same as what we've seen in the U.S. The Canadian dollar has moved a bit stronger and we should see more of that," said Wright.
Analysts said the increased expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will hold rates steady in July takes pressure off of the Bank of Canada and the Canadian dollar.
The currency had been under pressure from concerns the Bank of Canada might hold Canadian rates steady even as U.S. rates rose, drawing capital flows out of the country.
Canadian bond investors are now looking ahead to U.S. producer price index data for May being released tomorrow for confirmation that U.S. price pressures remain subdued.

In new issue news, the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corp on Thursday set C$400 million of 5.5 percent bonds due September 3, 2002 in financial markets. The bond was priced at 98.778 to yield 5.773, eight basis points over the Government of Canada's 5.5 percent bond due September, 2002.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.79 to C$107.20 to yield 6.266 percent while the U.S. 10-year rose 20/32 to 6.49 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to 22 basis points from 20 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.88 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 4.96 percent.
